app.name: AIEnv
app.subtitle: Home-region environment check
notice.purpose.title: Who this is for
notice.purpose.body: This tool is for overseas staff working in mainland China to check, and simulate, their overseas work network environment.
notice.risk.title: What this cannot promise
notice.risk.body: The tool only reduces exposure risk. It cannot guarantee that the account will not be flagged or banned. Claude does not offer service in mainland China, so you are responsible for following Claude's terms.
region.label: Home region
scan.hint: The scan reads this computer, then opens your default browser for WebRTC, language, and timezone signals. Nothing on the system is changed.
lang.label: Language
verdict.review: Review the warnings before relying on this environment
verdict.exposed: This environment does not look like the home region
phase.note: Phase 1 only detects and reports. Backup, restore, and repair are reserved for Phase 2 and do not change this computer.
empty.title: Choose the region this computer should resemble
empty.body: A scan compares exit IP, routing, DNS, time, language, and the real browser profile with that region.

browser.waiting: Waiting for the browser page. It usually finishes in a few seconds.
exit.missing: No IPv4 exit address was observed. Outbound checks may have been blocked.
exit.unlocated: The IPv4 exit {ip} could not be geolocated.
exit.mainland: The IPv4 exit {ip} is in mainland China ({place}).
exit.countryMismatch: The IPv4 exit {ip} is in {country} ({place}), not {expected}.
exit.okDatacenter: The IPv4 exit {ip} is in {expected} ({place}), but the network looks like a hosting or datacenter ASN ({org}).
exit.cityMismatch: The IPv4 exit {ip} is in {expected}, but the city is {city}, not {expectedCities}.
advice.exit.missing: Check that this computer can open outbound HTTPS, then scan again.
advice.exit.tunnel: Send this computer's traffic through a tunnel that exits in {expected}. A system proxy alone does not cover every app.
advice.exit.ok: No change suggested for the IPv4 exit country.
advice.exit.datacenter: Datacenter exits are easier to classify as proxy traffic. Prefer the residential or office egress your home region would actually use, if you have one.
advice.exit.city: Geolocated cities are often wrong for hosting addresses. Confirm the site in the tunnel provider's panel.
v6.none: There is no usable public IPv6 route, so IPv6 is not bypassing the tunnel.
v6.unmeasured: A public IPv6 route exists via {iface}, but the exit address could not be read.
v6.physicalLeak: IPv6 to the public internet uses the physical interface {iface} ({place}).
v6.physicalOk: IPv6 uses the physical interface {iface}, and the exit country is {expected}.
v6.unknown: IPv6 uses {iface}, which is neither a known tunnel nor a physical NIC.
advice.v6.keepOff: Leave public IPv6 disabled on the physical NIC while traveling, unless the tunnel carries IPv6 too.
advice.v6.tunnel: Move the IPv6 default route into the tunnel, or disable IPv6 on the physical NIC.
route.missing: No IPv4 route to the public internet was found.
route.tunnel: Public IPv4 traffic uses the tunnel interface {iface}.
route.physicalExposed: Public IPv4 traffic still uses the physical interface {iface}, and the exit is not {expected}.
route.physicalOk: Public IPv4 traffic uses the physical interface {iface}. The exit country matches {expected}, so this may be a direct connection rather than a travel tunnel.
route.split: Public probes took different interfaces ({ifaceA} and {ifaceB}).
route.unknown: Public IPv4 traffic uses {iface}, which is not a recognized tunnel or physical NIC.
advice.route.tunnel: Route public traffic through the tunnel interface. A proxy that only the browser uses leaves other apps on the local network.
advice.route.ok: No change suggested for the IPv4 route.
advice.route.missing: Check the default route, then scan again.
quic.tunnel: UDP, including QUIC on port 443, follows the tunnel interface {iface}. This is inferred from the routing table, not a live QUIC handshake.
quic.proxyBypass: A system proxy is on, but UDP to the public internet uses {iface}. QUIC can skip that proxy and expose the local network.
quic.direct: UDP to the public internet uses {iface}. HTTP proxies do not carry QUIC, so this path is direct.
quic.unknown: The UDP path could not be classified from interface {iface}.
quic.missing: No UDP route to the public internet was found.
advice.quic.block: Carry UDP/443 in the tunnel, or disable QUIC in the browser, so it cannot bypass an HTTP proxy.
advice.quic.missing: The route could not be read. If this matters, confirm with a local packet capture.
proxy.bypassAll: The proxy bypass list contains "*", so proxied apps do not use the proxy.
proxy.bypassClaude: The bypass list lets {entry} skip the proxy, which covers Claude or Anthropic.
proxy.pacHit: The PAC script mentions {entry}. It may send Claude or Anthropic direct.
proxy.pacUnread: An automatic proxy script is enabled ({url}), and its contents could not be read.
proxy.pacClean: An automatic proxy script is enabled and its text does not mention Claude or Anthropic. A script can still route around the proxy.
proxy.enabledClean: The system proxy is on, and the bypass list does not exempt Claude or Anthropic.
proxy.disabledTunnel: No system proxy is enabled. Public traffic is already on a tunnel interface.
proxy.disabledOpen: No system proxy is enabled, and public traffic is not on a tunnel interface.
advice.proxy.removeBypass: Remove Claude and Anthropic domains, and any wildcard, from the bypass list or PAC direct rules.
advice.proxy.readPac: Open the PAC file and confirm claude.ai and anthropic.com are not sent DIRECT.
advice.proxy.ok: No change suggested for the system proxy.
advice.proxy.enableOrTunnel: Turn on a tunnel for all apps, or a system proxy whose bypass list does not include Claude.
dns.none: No system DNS servers were found.
dns.fail: {count} configured resolver(s) are in mainland China or are known mainland public DNS: {detail}.
dns.local: Configured DNS is local or private ({detail}). That does not prove where queries are answered.
dns.ok: Configured public DNS is outside mainland China: {detail}.
dns.unknown: Configured DNS could not be classified: {detail}.
advice.dns.seeLeak: Use the resolver leak result, not only the configured address, to decide whether queries stay in mainland China.
advice.dns.replace: Point DNS at the resolver inside the tunnel, or at {recommended}, only after the exit country is already correct.
advice.dns.ok: No change suggested for configured DNS.
advice.dns.missing: Check DHCP or the VPN DNS settings, then scan again.
leak.fail: Recursive DNS answered from mainland China: {detail}.
leak.ok: Recursive DNS answered outside mainland China: {detail}.
leak.mismatch: Recursive DNS is outside mainland China but not in {expected}: {detail}.
leak.inconclusive: The resolver leak test did not return a recursive DNS server. This is not a pass.
advice.leak.fix: Stop the local resolver from answering in the wrong place. Use the tunnel's DNS or a resolver in {expected}.
advice.leak.ok: No change suggested for the resolver path.
advice.leak.retry: Scan again on a network that allows the leak test. A missing result is not evidence of safety.
ecs.absent: The resolver did not attach an EDNS client subnet.
ecs.ok: The reported client subnet {subnet} is in {expected}.
ecs.fail: The reported client subnet {subnet} is in mainland China.
ecs.mismatch: The reported client subnet {subnet} is in {country}, not {expected}.
ecs.unlocated: A client subnet {subnet} was reported, but it could not be geolocated.
ecs.unavailable: The EDNS client subnet probe did not get a response.
advice.ecs.ok: No change suggested for the client subnet.
advice.ecs.fix: Use a resolver that does not echo a mainland or third-country client subnet. Queries can reveal that subnet.
advice.ecs.retry: Try the scan again. Some networks block the Google diagnostic name.
tz.unknown: The system timezone could not be read.
tz.shanghai: The system timezone is Asia/Shanghai, which shows mainland China rather than {expected}.
tz.systemMismatch: The system timezone is {system}, which is not in the {expected} list ({allowed}).
tz.browserMismatch: The browser timezone is {browser}, which is not in the {expected} list.
tz.browserDiffers: The system timezone is {system} and the browser timezone is {browser}. They should match.
tz.ipDiffers: The exit IP geolocates to {ipTz}, outside the {expected} timezone list. The system timezone is {system}.
advice.tz.set: Set the system timezone to one used in {expected}, then restart the browser so Intl matches it.
advice.tz.ok: No change suggested for the timezone.
advice.tz.browser: Make the browser timezone follow the system timezone. Do not leave a page-level override behind.
locale.unknown: The system language could not be read.
locale.browserMismatch: The browser languages ({browser}) do not include {expected}.
locale.browserMissing: The system language matches {expected}, but the browser did not report languages.
advice.locale.set: Set the system language to {expected}, and align the browser's language list and Accept-Language with it.
advice.locale.browser: Add {expected} to the browser's preferred languages.
advice.locale.retryBrowser: Re-run the scan and let the local browser page finish.
webrtc.missing: The browser did not report WebRTC candidates.
webrtc.fail: WebRTC revealed a public address in {country}: {ip}.
webrtc.ok: WebRTC public addresses, when present, are in {expected}.
webrtc.localOnly: WebRTC did not reveal a public address. Local addresses seen: {ips}.
webrtc.none: WebRTC did not reveal any IP address.
advice.webrtc.disable: Disable non-proxied WebRTC, or force it through the tunnel, so it cannot reveal another country's address.
advice.webrtc.retry: Open the local check page in the default browser and let it finish, then scan again.
fp.missing: The browser did not report a fingerprint.
fp.webdriver: The browser reports navigator.webdriver, which is an automation flag.
fp.platform: The browser platform or user agent ({platform} / {uaOs}) does not match this {os} computer.
fp.lang: The browser languages and the system language do not overlap.
fp.tz: The browser timezone {browserTz} differs from the system timezone {systemTz}.
fp.ok: User agent, platform, and webdriver flag are consistent with this {os} computer.
advice.fp.webdriver: Use a normal browser window, not an automated or remote-debugging session.
advice.fp.platform: Use the browser that belongs on this operating system, without a spoofed user agent.
advice.fp.align: Align the browser language and timezone with the system.
advice.fp.ok: No change suggested for the browser fingerprint.
advice.fp.retry: Re-run the scan and let the local browser page finish.
loc.unknown: Location services and the browser geolocation permission could not be read.
loc.warnBrowser: The browser geolocation permission is already granted.
loc.prompt: The browser has not decided geolocation yet. A site can still ask.
loc.ok: System location services are off, and the browser has not granted geolocation.
advice.loc.off: Turn off system location services while traveling, and set the browser location permission to deny.
advice.loc.prompt: If a site asks for location, deny it.
clock.ok: The system clock is within {offset} of NTP.
clock.warn: The system clock is {offset} away from NTP.
clock.fail: The system clock is {offset} away from NTP.
clock.unavailable: NTP could not be queried, so clock skew was not measured.
advice.clock.sync: Enable automatic time sync and scan again.
advice.clock.ok: No change suggested for the clock.
advice.clock.retry: Allow outbound UDP/123 to an NTP server, or confirm the clock in system settings.
hosts.ok: The hosts file does not override Claude or Anthropic domains.
advice.hosts.remove: Remove those hosts entries so the domains resolve through the normal path.
advice.hosts.ok: No change suggested for the hosts file.
tls.suspicious: claude.ai presented a certificate from {issuer}, which looks like local TLS interception.
tls.unknown: claude.ai presented a certificate from {issuer}, which is not a recognized public CA for this check.
tls.unavailable: The certificate for claude.ai could not be read: {error}.
advice.tls.disableIntercept: Turn off HTTPS scanning, or the local interception certificate, for claude.ai.
advice.tls.ok: No change suggested for the certificate.
advice.tls.retry: Confirm this computer can complete a TLS handshake with claude.ai.
reach.ok: claude.ai responded in {claudeMs} ms and api.anthropic.com in {apiMs} ms. {detail}
advice.reach.fix: The tunnel or firewall is blocking these hosts. Reachability has to work before a browser session will.
